messages.subject: [FLR-list] Seasonal FLStock
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

There is at the moment no example of a seasonal FLStock in any FLR packages, although one needs to be added to FLasher, as it can forecast by season.

This is an object loaded from a seasonal SS3 SA model for Indian Ocean albacore tuna. The model has two sexes but this object has them collapsed

https://www.dropbox.com/s/bwijnp2b3ogjzbh/iotc_alb_sa2016.RData?dl=0

To create a seasonal object you need seasonal data. Remember seasons can be anything (months, weeks) but simply called then with sequential numbers (1:4, 1:12, 1:52), so that the order is clear.

If you pass to FLStock() an FLQuant with seasons, the whole object will have them:

stk <- FLStock(m=FQuant(0.1, dimnames=list(age=1:10, year=1980:2010, season=1:4)))

If you use ggplotFL, the plot of FLStock will take care of seasons. If you do plot(sa) after loading the example dataset above, you will see the seasonality in catches and ssb, but not in recruitment, as there is only recruitment in season 4.

Cheers,


Iago

messages.subject: [FLR-list] flash/flasher
messages.body_plain:
Hi,

FLash now compiles for Windows in R 64 bit only, and that is what is available at the repository for R 3.5.

FLasher is also 64 bit only. The main differences for the use are:

- Seasonal forecasting, needs seasonal targets.
- Separate units that differ in growth (e.g. sexes, spawning times)
- Separate ssb targets: ssb_spawn (at time of spawning), ssb_end (end of time step), and ssb_flash (FLash's trick of extending object one year if asking for ssb target when harvest.spwn = 0)
- Can project multiple stocks (FLBiols) and fisheries (FLFisheries, no metiers), still being tested fully, works with some mixfish examples.
- Includes SS3 bevholt stock-recruitment model.
- Better fwdControl() method, specially to deal with iterations in targets.
- Some small change to naming in target, val is now value, quantity is now quant.

On the TODO list for FLasher:

- Use different metrics of srp, not only ssb, on any SR model.
- This will allow use of SS3 low fecundity SRR, for example.
- Add more economic targets, only revenue is there right now.

I might be missing something, but those are the main differences I can remember now.

Cheers,


Iago
